top_signals.narrative: AMD expects server growth to accelerate significantly as it ramps up supply to meet increasing demand.
AMD's Q1 2026 GAAP diluted earnings per share was $0.84, an increase of 91% compared to Q1 2025.
AMD announced the production ramp of its next-generation EPYC processor, 'Venice,' utilizing TSMC's 2nm process technology.
Supermicro offers an expanded enterprise AI portfolio with over 100 GPU-optimized systems.
GPU cloud pricing at $3.50 via CoreWeave

watch_list.title: AMD 'Venice' EPYC processor production ramp
watch_list.rationale: The successful production ramp of AMD's next-generation 'Venice' EPYC processor is crucial for its market share in the server segment. Delays or faster-than-expected production can significantly impact AMD's revenue projections and competitive positioning against NVIDIA.
watch_list.trigger: Public statements from AMD or TSMC regarding the 'Venice' production timeline or volume. News reports on actual availability or initial customer deployments.

watch_list.title: Supermicro's enterprise AI portfolio expansion impact
watch_list.rationale: Supermicro's expanded portfolio and collaboration with NVIDIA indicate intensified competition in the enterprise AI market. Monitoring customer adoption rates and feedback on these new offerings will reveal their effectiveness in challenging AMD's server growth.
watch_list.trigger: Market reports on Supermicro's sales figures for its new GPU-optimized systems, or analyst commentary on the perceived success of their AI data platform solution.

watch_list.title: NVIDIA Blackwell Server Edition market reception
watch_list.rationale: NVIDIA's RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition offers a powerful alternative for AI and graphics workloads. Its market reception will indicate the level of competitive pressure AMD will face in high-performance computing and enterprise AI.
watch_list.trigger: Early reviews, benchmarks, or customer announcements regarding the adoption of the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition.

watch_list.title: Changes in GPU cloud pricing
watch_list.rationale: The current low GPU cloud pricing ($3.50/hr, H100 at $0.005/hr) from CoreWeave indicates a competitive market for AI compute. Any significant fluctuations in these prices could signal shifts in supply/demand dynamics or new competitive strategies impacting both AMD and NVIDIA.
watch_list.trigger: Reports or announcements from cloud providers like CoreWeave or others regarding changes in their GPU instance pricing for current generation or next-generation hardware.
